reuse.why: Replaces the scattered getDateWithSkippedWeekend calls with one WeekendRule-based applyWeekendRule plus isSkippedWeekendOccurrence. All callers (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, the new getDatesInRange and both template sites) use it, and the new handler reuses recurConfigToRSchedule and RSchedule.

duplication.why: The weekend/holiday decision is shared. Two things are still repeated: the occurrence look-ahead padding is worked out separately in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and the filter-skipped-then-apply pipeline appears in both handlers.

placement.why: Rule definitions live in shared/schedules.ts, handlers in server/schedules/app.ts and the type in RecurConfig, following the tree's layering.

scope.why: Every edit serves one of the five steps; there are no unrelated changes.

maintainability.why: The rule object is a reasonable single definition. The three ad-hoc lookahead formulas are fragile, though, and applyWeekendRule silently returns daily dates unchanged, so callers must also remember to call isSkippedWeekendOccurrence.

disguised_duplication.where: The bounded look-ahead for skipped weekend/holiday occurrences is reshaped three ways: DAILY_WEEKEND_LOOKAHEAD * (1 + holidays) in getNextDate, count * 2 + 7 + holidays in getUpcomingDates, and 3 * (1 + holidays) padding in getDatesInRange. All three express the same concern without a shared helper.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule grew frequency and holidays fields. applyWeekendRule gained a daily-frequency early return, and isHoliday gained a recurring MM-DD special case. getNextDate wraps the helper in its own `noSkipWeekend ? date : applyWeekendRule(...)` branch.
